question: How many named storms will the 2026 Pacific hurricane season have recorded as of October 29, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Wikipedia infobox shows 22 named storms as of Oct 19 (Trudy latest, now a TS; Vance/Winnie unused). NHC 11am PDT Oct 19 EPac TWO gives EP94 south of Guatemala 60%/48h and 90%/7d, TD expected mid-week -> ~85% it becomes Vance by Oct 29. A 24th storm would need a second genesis in the remaining ~10 days of late October; this hyperactive El Nino season makes that plausible (~20%), but climatology declines sharply after mid-Oct. A central Pacific named storm is a small additional tail. Market check: Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi searches found no matching contract (none found). A fan-wiki 'Vance Oct 20-22' result is a hypothetical page and was ignored.
calls.dossier:
- Wikipedia '2026 Pacific hurricane season' infobox (fetched 2026-10-19): Total storms 22; latest Trudy (formed Oct 13, still active, now a tropical storm offshore west-central Mexico), Simon (Oct 7); Rachel Sep 27; TD Nineteen-E Sep 29 (unnamed). Central Pacific named: Lala, Moke, Nolo (already in the count). Vance, Winnie unused.
- NHC EPac TWO, 11 AM PDT Oct 19 2026: EP94, a trough/low several hundred miles SW of Guatemala, moving W-WNW ~10 mph and staying well offshore; formation 60% in 48h, 90% in 7 days; conditions conducive; TD expected around mid-week (Oct 21-22). No other areas were listed in the fetched summary.
- Latin Times Oct 17: Trudy peaked Cat 3; season had 22 named storms, 12 hurricanes, 9-10 majors, record ACE (~337), above 2018.
- Season context: hyperactive EPac with a strong El Nino (Atlantic quiet, 9 storms). The Atlantic subtropical low near the Carolinas does not affect this count.
- Note: a fan 'hypotheticalhurricanes' wiki page describes a fictional 'TS Vance Oct 20-22'. It is not evidence.
- Climatology: EPac formation rates decline after mid-October; the 1991-2020 average is ~15 named storms per season. Late-Oct/early-Nov storms do occur (e.g., Vance 2014 formed Oct 30). In active El Nino years a 10-day late-October window often holds 0-1 formations; 2 is uncommon.
- NHC 90%/7d probabilities refer to TD-or-stronger genesis. A TD that forms over warm water in a conducive environment usually but not always reaches TS strength.
- Resolution: resolves off the Wikipedia infobox 'Total storms' at 23:59 UTC Oct 29 (fallback: NHC), not off ACE or hurricane counts. Wikipedia infobox editing lag is typically hours.
- Event window: cumulative season count through 2026-10-29 23:59 UTC. As of Oct 19 18Z, ~10.2 days remain. The count is currently 22 and cannot fall barring reanalysis.
- Market search: none found on Polymarket, Manifold, or Kalshi for this count.
- Searched but not found: model-guidance (GFS/ECMWF) genesis signals for a second system after EP94; a CPHC outlook for central Pacific activity.

At 11 AM PDT Oct 19 the NHC gave EP94 60% in 48h and 90% in 7d, with a TD expected mid-week over a favorable environment. That leaves about a week to reach TS strength, so P(Vance named by Oct 29) is about 0.83. A second genesis in the remaining ~10 days of late October is about 0.15. Climatology declines after mid-October, but this is a hyperactive El Nino season, and EP94 already uses part of the window. Market check: none found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.
calls.reconciliation: All three dossiers agree on the facts: infobox 22, Vance unused, EP94 at 60%/90% with a TD expected mid-week, no markets, and a fan-wiki 'Vance' page that is fiction and should be disregarded. There was no factual dispute to settle. The only differences are judgment calls: P(EP94 named) at 0.80-0.85 and P(an extra storm) at 0.15-0.20. Given the 90% 7-day odds and the ~7-day naming runway, I take 0.83 and 0.15 as the readings I would bet on. I carry forward the runs' reference class and their roughly 1.8 dispersion. Upper escape above 26.5 needs 4+ new storms in 10 days and is negligible, so I omit it.
